items.status: FIXED — native-53, Order 53 (close at the merge)
items.title: F129's order did not reach a call through a closure VALUE: `check(items, push())` (`check` a closure binding, `push` pushing into the captured `items`) printed `true` on JS and `false` natively; `measure(&words, more())` 2 / 1; `count_of(&total, add())` 5 / 0
items.body: vilan-rust's `closure_call_arguments` rendered every argument in order, so F129's deferred copy of an argument rooted at a captured `mut` binding (spec §6.9's view) never applied to a closure binding, a field holding a closure or a function item's binding. It now asks `defers_its_cell_copy` as a named callee does and settles the other code-running arguments in `let`s first; the JS transformer reads the argument late through a closure value too (F138's rule without cell views). A computed callee (`make()(..)`) and a literal applied where it is written (natively inlined as `let`s) keep their order on both. Estate 0 (corpus and kolt native emission byte-identical). Pin `a_closure_value_call_reads_a_captured_binding_after_the_later_arguments_on_both_backends`.

items.kind: diagnostics (checker hole; native backend defect message)
items.title: A `&mut` receiver over a binding no closure captures, beside a later argument that RE-BINDS the receiver's root (`log.items.push({ log = fresh(); 9 })`, `log.bump({ log = fresh(); 9 })`), checks clean; JS writes the object `log` held when the receiver was evaluated (prints 0) and the native emission is refused by rustc (E0506, reported as a BACKEND defect)
items.body: Spec §6.4 (rule 4: no invalidating mutation under a live view) reads the argument as a reassignment of the `&mut` view's root while the view is live — the view is taken where the receiver stands. The captured-binding twin is F138's (both backends now take the view after the later arguments and write the new binding). Rec: a checker refusal at the rebind (`log` is re-bound while `log.items` is lent `&mut` to this call — settle the value first: `let item = { log = fresh(); 9 }; log.items.push(item)`), estate counted first (expected 0); the alternative — reading an uncaptured binding's `&mut` place after the later arguments too — would make §6.9's order a rule of every binding, not of captured ones.

items.title: A module-level `mut` binding handed to a call beside a later argument that writes it answers differently: `has(global, grow())` (`grow` pushing into `global`) prints `true` on JS and `false` natively; `lent(&global, grow())` the same; `global.push(reset())` (`reset` re-binding `global`) leaves 1 item on JS and 2 natively
items.body: F129/F138's order is §6.9's, for CAPTURED bindings; a module-level `mut` binding is a place every function shares, and neither backend orders its arguments by that. Natively a by-value or `&` argument over it is copied out of its thread-local cell where it stands (so an in-place write by a later argument is missed, where the JS argument is the binding's object), and a `&mut` receiver over it borrows the cell after the hoisted by-value arguments (so a re-binding is seen, where JS writes the old object). Rec: the same rule as F138 for a module-level `mut` binding — read late on both when a later argument runs code (any call can reach the binding) — the estate counted first; the native half is `defers_its_cell_copy`'s `cell_spine` admitting a module root, the JS half `argument_order.rs`'s `is_captured` answering true for one.
